title: A topic SVD and a hidden chain
summary: Latent semantic analysis, and the probabilities an HMM and Viterbi use.

choices.text: Latent semantic analysis factorizes a term-document matrix by truncated SVD. The fit does not use document labels, and a new document is folded in by projecting its term vector with the term singular vectors already learned.
In a first-order HMM the next hidden state depends on the current state and on the previous observation, which is what makes the emissions informative.
Viterbi computes, for every time step, the posterior probability of each hidden state by summing over all paths, while forward-backward returns the single most likely path.
In a first-order hidden Markov model the hidden state is Markov, with transitions P(state_t | state_{t−1}), and the observation is drawn from an emission P(observation_t | state_t).
Latent semantic analysis needs a label on every document, because its truncated SVD is fit to separate the classes, as in linear discriminant analysis.
